stem: A test evaluation labels the four groups as A = true positive, B = false positive, C = false negative and D = true negative. Which of the following ratios measures the fraction of actual cases that the test detects?

options.label: A
options.explanation: This ratio is specificity, since it counts true negatives among all people without disease. The requested detection fraction instead starts with the actual cases, represented by A and C.
options.misconception: Uses the specificity formula when detection among actual cases is requested.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This ratio counts false positives among all positive results. It measures errors within the positive-test group rather than the fraction of actual cases successfully detected.
options.misconception: Counts false discoveries within positives instead of detected cases within disease.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Actual cases consist of true positives plus false negatives, A + C. The detected cases are A, so sensitivity is A divided by A + C.
options.misconception: No misconception: A plus C includes both detected and missed actual cases.

options.label: D
options.explanation: This ratio counts missed cases among all negative results. Sensitivity instead asks how many actual cases are detected, using the case group rather than negative results as the denominator.
options.misconception: Uses missed cases among negative results rather than detected cases among all cases.

options.label: E
options.explanation: This ratio is positive predictive value: true cases among all positive results. Sensitivity uses all actual cases, including missed cases, as its denominator instead.
options.misconception: Confuses the positive-result denominator with the actual-case denominator.

context:
Learning objective: Build the sensitivity denominator from true positives plus false negatives before interpreting screening results.

Actual cases consist of true positives plus false negatives, A + C. The detected cases are A, so sensitivity is A divided by A + C.
